description: An account's region is the region of the branch where the account is held.

a.request: For each account with standing orders, count its orders, grouping by account id (`order.account_id`) and the region (`district.A3`) of the branch district where the account is held (`account.district_id`), not where its owner lives. Work out how far each account's order count is above or below the average count across all these account–region rows. Then average those differences within each region, and keep only the accounts whose difference is greater than their region's average difference. Show the account id, region, number of orders, difference from the overall average, and how much that difference exceeds the region's average difference. Sort by that last value from highest to lowest, return only the top 10, and don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH account_orders AS (SELECT o.account_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM `order` AS o JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = o.account_id JOIN district AS d ON d.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY o.account_id, d.A3), differences AS (SELECT account_id, region, order_count, order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM account_orders) AS difference_from_overall_average FROM account_orders), regional_differences AS (SELECT account_id, region, order_count, difference_from_overall_average, AVG(difference_from_overall_average) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS region_average_difference FROM differences) SELECT account_id, region, order_count, difference_from_overall_average, difference_from_overall_average - region_average_difference AS excess_over_region_average FROM regional_differences WHERE difference_from_overall_average > region_average_difference ORDER BY excess_over_region_average DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: For each account with standing orders, count its orders, grouping by account id (`order.account_id`) and the account's region (`district.A3`). Work out how far each account's order count is above or below the average count across all these account–region rows. Then average those differences within each region, and keep only the accounts whose difference is greater than their region's average difference. Show the account id, region, number of orders, difference from the overall average, and how much that difference exceeds the region's average difference. Sort by that last value from highest to lowest, return only the top 10, and don't round anything. An account's region is the region of the branch where the account is held.
c.sql: WITH account_orders AS (SELECT o.account_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM `order` AS o JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = o.account_id JOIN district AS d ON d.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY o.account_id, d.A3), differences AS (SELECT account_id, region, order_count, order_count - AVG(order_count) OVER () AS difference_from_overall_average FROM account_orders), regional_differences AS (SELECT account_id, region, order_count, difference_from_overall_average, difference_from_overall_average - AVG(difference_from_overall_average) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS excess_over_region_average FROM differences) SELECT account_id, region, order_count, difference_from_overall_average, excess_over_region_average FROM regional_differences WHERE excess_over_region_average > 0 ORDER BY excess_over_region_average DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: For each account with at least one standing order, use its branch district’s region, count its orders, and subtract the unrounded average order count across all account–region rows; within each region, average those differences, retain accounts whose difference exceeds that regional average, and return the account ID, region, order count, difference from the overall average, and excess over the regional average, sorted by excess descending and limited to 10 rows
b.sql: WITH account_orders AS (SELECT a.account_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM account AS a JOIN district AS d ON d.district_id = a.district_id JOIN `order` AS o ON o.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY a.account_id, d.A3), differences AS (SELECT account_id, region, order_count, order_count - AVG(order_count) OVER () AS difference_from_overall_average FROM account_orders), regional_averages AS (SELECT region, AVG(difference_from_overall_average) AS regional_average_difference FROM differences GROUP BY region) SELECT x.account_id, x.region, x.order_count, x.difference_from_overall_average, x.difference_from_overall_average - r.regional_average_difference AS excess_over_regional_average FROM differences AS x JOIN regional_averages AS r ON r.region = x.region WHERE x.difference_from_overall_average > r.regional_average_difference ORDER BY excess_over_regional_average DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: For each account with standing orders, count its orders, grouping by `order.account_id` and the region (`district.A3`) of the branch where the account is held. Calculate each account’s order count minus the average count across all account–region rows. Then average those differences within each region and keep only accounts whose difference exceeds their region’s average. Show the account id, region, order count, difference from the overall average, and amount by which that difference exceeds the region’s average. Sort by the last value descending, return the top 10, and do not round any values.
d.sql: WITH account_orders AS (SELECT o.account_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM `order` AS o JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = o.account_id JOIN district AS d ON d.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY o.account_id, d.A3), differences AS (SELECT account_id, region, order_count, order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM account_orders) AS difference_from_overall_average FROM account_orders), region_averages AS (SELECT region, AVG(difference_from_overall_average) AS region_average_difference FROM differences GROUP BY region) SELECT diff.account_id, diff.region, diff.order_count, diff.difference_from_overall_average, diff.difference_from_overall_average - ra.region_average_difference AS excess_over_region_average FROM differences AS diff JOIN region_averages AS ra ON ra.region = diff.region WHERE diff.difference_from_overall_average > ra.region_average_difference ORDER BY excess_over_region_average DESC LIMIT 10;
